title: Say No To Blood Tech (Apples Against Apartheid)
content:
A post shared by Labor4Palestine (@labor4palestine)

Our fourth global event is here: Say No to Blood Tech! On October 23, we are calling on communities worldwide to picket their local Apple Stores in response to the company’s infatuation with Israel. While Apple fans obsess over the duo, it’s our job to educate them about how bloody that phone really is.

And because Apple is also guilty of complicity in the Congolese genocide, we are partnering with @congofriends & @teamcongo.rdc to bring awareness of the issues within the company’s supply chain.

We’re making it super easy for you to show up next month:

Go to our website, pick your flyers & posters, print them, and show up on October to picket! Use the hashtags #saynotobloodtech and #applepicking, and tag us the day you show up.

Are you a local organizer or org that wants to get involved? Contact us through our website.

This is going to be the world’s largest global protest event against big tech — show up and be a part of history! #apple#iphone duo

author: labor4pal
title: What is driving the shift on Palestine and war in the unions? (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
In the run up to this year’s TUC conference, over 1,500 people signed a petition in support of the UCU motion asking the TUC to reaffirm its support for a position of “wages not weapons”

The TUC union federation conference this month carried motions that promoted a progressive position on war and Palestine.

The UCU union’s motion built upon last year’s “wages not weapons”, which officially ended the TUC’s policy of support for increasing arms spending.

This motion was opposed by only a handful of unions, albeit powerful ones such as Unite, GMB, Prospect and Community whose members work in defence.

On Palestine, TUC conference backed a motion brought by the AUE union that called to support the Palestinian-led Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement.

The motions carried reflect a significant shift that has taken place within the trade union movement.

TUC delegates are mainly made up of full-time officials not known for their radicalism. Days before the conference began TUC general secretary Paul Nowak launched an attack on the UCU motion.

He argued that “welfare not warfare” is a right wing slogan, arguing that the progressive position is welfare and warfare.

This was an attempt to shore up opposition to the motion to bring the TUC in line with the Labour government’s policy of increasing defence spending.

author: labor4pal
title: How Federal Agents Surveilled a Worker Assembly in Minneapolis (Workday Magazine)
content:
By Amie Stager | September 23, 2026

On February 15, during Operation Metro Surge and following the January 23 economic shutdown, around 400 people from the Twin Cities gathered at the United Labor Centre in Minneapolis for a workers’ assembly on building the movement against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). According to newly released documents in the case against the Minnesota 15, who were indicted in June and charged with conspiracy for alleged anti-ICE activity, undercover federal agents were present at the assembly, and reported on the minute workings of the gathering.

Two documents, both submitted to the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota as exhibits in the case, are transcripts of recordings between two special agents and two unnamed undercover agents surveilling the worker assembly. One is three pages long and one is eight pages, and they include summaries of the debate and discourse that took place, and pejorative remarks about the appearances of some speakers at the assembly. They also show that agents did not appear to have a deep understanding of some of the oppressed and exploited community members who were present at the assembly. author: labor4pal
title: After the Strike: The Battle for the Story of Minneapolis (Workers Resist)
content:
December 2025 and January 2026 were difficult months in the Twin Cities metro. Operation Metro Surge cast a shadow over daily life, touching nearly everyone in one way or another. Maybe you were an immigrant from Ecuador without papers, afraid to even go outside. Or an educator who saw their students’ lives torn apart by the abduction of a parent. It could be that you were one of those residents that served as a legal observer and got pepper-sprayed and arrested by ICE agents. For everyone in Minneapolis and St. Paul, that time was insane, like living in a war zone.

Of course residents didn’t take the military occupation of our neighborhoods and communities lying down. Working-class people fought back by organizing themselves into massive rapid-response and mutual-aid networks throughout the metro. Every week saw demonstrations in the streets, as the working-class pushed back. Then Rene Good was murdered, and it was clear that this was something on a scale that no one had experienced before.

SEIU Local 26 led the way, along with two local nonprofits, in calling for a day of “No Work, No School, No Shopping” on January 23. title: Port Elizabeth 4: Human Rights Are Never Abstract
content:
A post shared by Port of Elizabeth Movement (P.O.E.M) (@port.of.elizabeth.movement)

⚓️The Port Elizabeth 4 will have their trial on Monday, September 14th, 9 am, at 1 Police Plaza, Elizabeth, New Jersey. A 30-minute press conference will precede the trial, and that will be at 8:30am.⚓️🚨

🚨⚓️The trial had been scheduled two previous times and postponed with very short notice. On October 3, 2025, the four arrestees were part of an autonomous coalition of 100 protestors who stopped trucks delivering 1,000 tons of military weapons to the Port of Elizabeth bound that week for Israel. Cargo included 61 tons of forging rings, which can be used for artillery shells and military/aerospace applications.⚓️🚨

🚨⚓️Their charges include “obstruction of roadways” and “failure to comply in presence of riot”, precisely what was necessary to block military cargo from being illegally used for genocide. The 4 activists, Teresa Grady, Danny Creamer, Ellen Grady and Mark Scibilia-Carver, who placed themselves at risk, will represent themselves and use defenses of necessity, and, US and international law.⚓️🚨

Palestinian Unions: Global Call for Worker Action Against Genocide this November

Author info Palestinian Trade Unions

The Palestinian labor movement reiterates its solidarity with workers across the world resisting all forms of oppression and calls for global action to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing genocide and apartheid from Friday, November 20th leading up to the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People on Sunday, November 29th 2026.

This coming November, we the undersigned Palestinian trade unions and federations urgently renew our call to unions around the world to:

Uphold and defend the inalienable rights of the Indigenous people of Palestine as stipulated in international law, particularly the right of our refugees to return home and receive reparations, and

Escalate BDS pressure to end all state, corporate and institutional complicity in Israel’s illegal occupation, apartheid and genocide.

While approaching the third anniversary of the beginning of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People, and in light of Israel’s accelerating ethnic cleansing, annexation, settler violence and pogroms in the West Bank, and depraved violent repression of our prisoners, we remind ourselves that an injury to one is an injury to all.
